title: retrieval-truncation-sink-exploratory-eval
content:
Purpose:
This note captures exploratory experiments and early regression checks for long-context + retrieval stress tests across 8k, 32k, and 128k target windows. The goal is to surface pathologies (truncation points, retrieval insertion interactions, attention sink behaviors) that can silently regress when we change KV cache indexing, chunked attention, or retrieval insertion position logic.

Background and Motivation:
- Several regressions have been reported in recent private deployments where previously-stable models began dropping context after large retrieval insertions. Root causes suspected: off-by-one in chunk boundaries, KV-cache pointer drift after chunked attention, and tokenization boundary mismatches when retrieval items include unusual punctuation.
- We need a reproducible, small battery of probes (deterministic prompts + synthetic retrievals) that we can run in CI and during model onboarding to flag attention-sink and truncation regressions.

Experiment Matrix (high-level):
- Model variants: baseline-v1 (current prod), quant-8-v2 (8-bit), kernel-change-2024-11
- Context targets: 8k, 32k, 128k (measured in model context tokens)
- Retrieval insertion styles: append-at-end, interleave-every-512, insert-in-middle (token index approx 16384 for 32k), sliding-window (rolling recent docs)
- Prompt families: 
  1) email-long-thread-8k: simulated stacked replies and multiple quoted segments to test prefix retention
  2) policy-manual-32k: multi-section policy doc with numbered headings; retrieval returns sections with same headings (tests aliasing and dedup)
  3) depo-128k: long deposition transcripts with speaker tags and timecodes (tests large offsets and repetition)
- Metrics to record (automated): truncation_point_token (if any), earliest_loss_of_reference (token index where model no longer references ground-truth anchor), hallucination_rate (binary flags per probe), rerank_score_drop (for retrieval alignment), attention_mass_to_retrieved (diagnostic scalar we compute from attention weights to retrieval spans)

Prompt and Retrieval Construction:
- Retrieval documents purposely include header duplication and near-duplicate paragraphs to test de-dup logic. Examples: repeated clause ‘Section 2.3 — Confidentiality’ occurs twice with minor edits.
- To create consistent token counts, we use the internal tokenization script used by the runtime (scripts/tokenize_for_evals.py) so counts reflect runtime behavior.
- For 128k probes we build a long synthetic transcript by concatenating 400 short snippets (average 300 tokens) with occasional injected integers and timecode markers to create attention anchors.

Attention-sink diagnostic procedure (quick):
1) Run forward through model keeping per-layer attention maps (downsample if memory-heavy; target layers 6/12/last-4).
2) Compute attention_mass_to_retrieved = sum(attention from decoding tokens to retrieval tokens) normalized by decoding token attention mass. Track at sliding buckets of 256 tokens.
3) Flag sink if attention_mass_to_retrieved drops >80% across a consecutive 1024-token span while expected anchor tokens still exist.
4) Correlate with top-k KV-cache pointers to ensure pointer drift is not the primary cause.

Key Observations (exploratory run notes):
- 8k suite: mostly stable. Two edge cases: 
  * When retrieval insertion occurs at characters that split a token (rare punctuation patterns), the model occasionally treats the retrieval as separate authoring (drops anchor reference after ~120 tokens). Hypothesis: token boundary mismatch caused retrieval to be tokenized differently by client vs runtime.
  * Small repetition loops in email threads (e.g., repeated ‘On Tue…’) sometimes cause attention to concentrate on the repeated header — minor degradation but recoverable.
- 32k suite: several interesting failures. 
  * Insert-in-middle at token ~16384 produced a reproducible attention collapse in kernel-change-2024-11 build: attention_mass_to_retrieved drops sharply after ~2048 tokens of decoding and never recovers. KV-cache pointers show a shift of +1 at chunk boundary.
  * Sliding-window style retrieval (rolling recent docs) with overlapping content resulted in duplicated context being treated as conflicting signals; the model alternated between two slightly different versions of the same paragraph.
- 128k suite: stress uncovered two distinct classes of failure. 
  * Memory pressure triggers fallback that truncates oldest retrievals without updating the local prompt-tracking metadata — leads to invisible truncation where user sees full prompt but runtime has dropped items.
  * Attention dilution: as decoding progresses past 90k tokens, attention mass to original anchor steadily diffuses across many repeated snippets, increasing hallucination_rate on grounding tasks by ~12% relative to baseline.

Repro Steps for a 32k failing case (kernel-change-2024-11):
1) Checkout runtime branch: git checkout kernel-change-2024-11; run local docker image build (instructions in linked PR).
2) Load test harness: python eval_harness.py --prompt-set policy-manual-32k --retrieval-mode insert-in-middle --seed 42 --capture-attn true --output results/32k-kernel-change.json
3) Inspect results/32k-kernel-change.json: check attention_mass_to_retrieved trend and KV-cache pointer map in metadata. Expected: drop at ~2048 tokens produced by branch commit 6f3a2b1.

Regression gates proposed (CI-friendly):
- Deterministic probes: 6 short deterministic prompts per context size (8k/32k/128k) executed on every runtime change that touches kv-cache or attention kernels. Fail CI if any probe shows: 
  * truncation_point_token is earlier than baseline by >256 tokens OR 
  * attention_mass_to_retrieved decreases by >60% relative to baseline for >=512 consecutive tokens OR
  * hallucination_rate delta >8% absolute.
- Baseline storage: store JSON snapshots (attention summaries, kv pointers) for last-green commit per model variant. Compare via a hashing utility (scripts/compare_eval_snapshots.py).

Action items and owners:
- Asha: add tokenization round-trip check in client retrieval pipeline to ensure retrieval items match runtime tokenization (due 2025-01-20).
- Liam: wire deterministic 32k probe into CI; initial run target 5 consecutive builds (due 2025-01-26).
- Marisol (me): prepare a compact 128k diagnostic that fits within 10GB mem cap by selectively downsampling attention layers; add to nightly runs (due 2025-02-02).
- Sofia: audit retrieval dedup logic for overlapping sliding windows and propose a canonical merge rule (due 2025-01-22).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we prefer a client-side canonicalization step (dedupe by normalized whitespace + semantic hash) before storage, or rely on runtime merge? Tradeoffs: client canonicalization reduces I/O but may prevent runtime from using raw source ordering.
- Is the current KV-cache pointer format resilient to chunk reordering? If not, propose small compact metadata (window_id + offset) to be included with inserted retrievals.

Appendix: sample probe snippets (verbatim examples)
- policy-manual-32k snippet (short):
  "Section 4.2 — Data retention policy: All logs retained up to 36 months unless flagged for deletion. See Appendix F for legal exceptions."
- depo-128k speaker snippet (short):
  "Q: And on July 12, you logged that the device rebooted at 11:07?
   A: Yes, it rebooted, then we reconnected and the service resumed."

Notes to reviewers:
- This is exploratory; I expect more tuning on the heuristic thresholds for sink detection. Please run the attached harness against your local kernel-change branches and paste results into DOC-1427 for tracking.

Last tested on: kernel-change-2024-11 with model baseline-v1; seed 42; local infra (dev-gpu-03).
